business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Andean Community Commercial Integration Framework (Cartagena Agreement)
Colombia–Spain Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 2014, effective 2016)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF framework); Law 1121 of 2006 (financing of terrorism); Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. rules); Decree 830 of 2020 (as amended by Decree 1952 of 2021) on final beneficiaries; Superintendencia de Sociedades Resolution 2020-01-137317 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); Circular Básica Jurídica of Superintendencia Financiera and UIAF directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation for corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention of 1961) or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a party to the Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granting incorporation authority to the Colombian attorney or incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or equivalent public officer in the grantor's jurisdiction of domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy or official government-issued identification of each ultimate beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or national identity registry of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board of Directors or shareholders' resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Colombian S.A.S. and appointment of initial officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, notary, or authorized officer(s) of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of corporate records, certified in accordance with local corporate law

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Colombian domestic lists (including the UIAF and the Superintendencia de Sociedades registry of persons subjected to restrictive measures); and (v) the national PEP database. Screening results must be documented in the incorporation file and updated at least quarterly or upon any change in beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – Confecámaras; administered locally by the authorized Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be written in Spanish or using Latin alphabetic characters; names based on non-Latin scripts require transliteration to the Latin alphabet. Spanish-language accent marks and special characters are generally permitted but discouraged for commercial interoperability. The S.A.S. descriptor must be included or added as a suffix. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing trade name, distinctive sign, or company name registered in the RUES database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration motion (recurso de reposición) before the same Registration Commission of the Cámara de Comercio within ten (10) working days of notification. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a supplementary appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within ten (10) working days. In parallel, the applicant may confirm availability of a secondary alternate name to protect the timeline. At any stage, the applicant may submit a corrected name proposal rather than continue an administrative appeal, provided the proposed name is not prospectively confusing with prior registrations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally accepted for an S.A.S. engaged in automated dropshipping, provided the registered office is located within Colombian national territory, enables effective receipt of legal notices, and the tax administration has a valid physical address for inspection records. Dropshipping with no local inventory reduces the need for a physical warehouse; a commercial agent or law-firm address may be used as the registered office. The Colombian Commercial Registry will reject an address that is merely a post-office box or a non-existent location. Banks may impose stricter physical address requirements during corporate account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10–15% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Superintendencia de Sociedades or the tax administration for a medium-risk dropshipping entity, primarily triggered by inconsistent reported income or anomalous UBO declarations. The likelihood increases to 25–30% if the company is selected for transfer pricing review or applies for VAT refunds without supporting commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Confecámaras registration tariffs

Apostille of foreign documents (average per document, assuming Hague Convention jurisdiction)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee or Hague Apostille fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for virtual/commercial office arranging and corporate address obligations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio), Articles 110, 353-372; Decree 1074 of 2015 (Single Regulatory Decree on Commerce), Articles concerning merchant registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de la jurisdicción del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), under the oversight of the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) registered in the Mercantile Registry; public deed required if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for an S.A.S.; the incorporating shareholders may subscribe zero or nominal capital. If capital is specified, it must be fully paid within two years from incorporation. No escrow account is mandated by Colombian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial share subscription of the Company under the S.A.S. regime as set forth in Law 1258 of 2008 is hereby approved and acknowledged in accordance with the subscribed capital schedule, without requiring immediate payment of capital contributions, subject to payment within the two-year statutory term. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is established at the address recorded in the bylaws, and that all statutory books and corporate records shall be maintained at such address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed: a General Manager (Representante Legal) and a Secretary, each with the powers and limits contained in the bylaws. RESOLVED, that all actions taken pursuant to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-validation of corporate name and homonymy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) – online homonymy search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Chamber’s website, enter one or more proposed corporate names, pay the nominal search fee, and obtain the homonymy certificate confirming that no identical registered mercantile name exists in the same jurisdiction. Keep the certificate for use within its 30-day validity window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the desired name is rejected due to conflict, file a new homonymy request with an alternative name or add a distinctive suffix; no penalty applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SAS private incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (for signature authentication) or certified digital signature provider via the VUCE portal; final registration at Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the ‘documento privado de constitución’ under Law 1258 of 2008, containing the bylaws, shareholder subscriptions, capital structure, legal representative designation, and registered office. The document must be executed by all initial shareholders, with signatures notarized or affixed by certified digital signature. If real estate is contributed, the incorporation must be executed by public deed before a notary.
required_dossiers: Private incorporation document (or public deed if real property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber observes form errors, re-execute or amend the document and resubmit; a corrected signature page may be accepted without full re-incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Mercantile Registry and issuance of certificate of existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de la jurisdicción del domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated incorporation document and related forms with the Chamber, pay the registration fee calculated on subscribed capital, and obtain the ‘Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal’. This certificate is the conclusive proof of legal formation and must be kept current.
required_dossiers: Payment of registration and enrollment fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is queried, correct the deficiency indicated in the official response within the Chamber’s administrative deadline and resubmit; if the certificate contains errors, request a partial amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with DIAN and NIT issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) application using the Chamber-issued certificate, selecting income tax, VAT, and electronic invoicing obligations relevant to e-commerce. The NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) will be generated automatically; download the RUT certificate as proof of taxpayer status.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT application requests additional information, provide the missing data through the MUISCA portal; if the NIT is issued without desired tax code classifications, file a RUT correction (actualización) immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the corporate transaction account and enabling payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Colombian financial entity under the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (e.g., large banks such as Bancolombia and Davivienda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate formation bundle to the chosen bank and request a checking account in the company’s name, with the legal representative or sub-authorized users enabled for payment gateways Stripe/PayPal settlements. Strict KYC/AML due diligence applies; source of funds and ownership declaration must be provided.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, submit a notarized source-of-funds declaration and commercial projection; if the bank rejects the risk profile, open the account at another supervised entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization of corporate books and governance filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Physically or electronically present the corporate ledgers (shareholder register, board minutes book, or electronic book system) for legalization by the Chamber. Maintain the books at the registered office and record the initial board resolution, share subscriptions and any subsequent board actions once approved.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
Initial board resolution and shareholder consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If books fail sealing inspection due to formatting, amend the ledger format, repurchase approved book models, and resubmit for legalization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) exercises consumer protection and e-commerce regulation; no industrial or prior operating license is mandatory for automated dropshipping activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the automated dropshipping business; the activity is classified as non-manufacturing retail through internet platforms. If physical warehouse space is later adopted, municipal commercial zoning permits and fire safety certificates may apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible and regional Autonomous Regional Corporations (CARs)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA required for virtual dropshipping without industrial installations; no significant environmental impact expected.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the virtual business model; any leased office or logistics space must comply with municipal solid waste disposal regulations and, if applicable, minimum commercial waste handling standards under Colombian environmental rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a purely virtual dropshipping operation, no structural load inspection or civil defense clearance is required. If a physical office or warehouse is opened, a fire safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) and basic workplace safety registration (Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo) must be obtained from the relevant municipal authority and ARL insurer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); taxpayer portals: MUISCA (https://muisca.dian.gov.co) and RUT registration at https://www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic formation path: file articles of incorporation (public deed or private written instrument) at the Cámara de Comercio of the registered office; the S.A.S. then enrolls in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through DIAN's MUISCA platform immediately upon commercial registration and before starting activities, obtaining the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). Foreign-owned S.A.S. variant: appoint a legal representative domiciled in Colombia, complete the commercial registry formalities (including foreign-company or shareholder registration), execute the RUT enrolment and NIT issuance through MUISCA in the name of the entity, and activate DIAN-certified electronic invoicing before issuing the first invoice. The NIT is the unified number for income tax, VAT, customs operations, e-invoicing, and payroll.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no check-the-box regime; every S.A.S. is an entity-level CIT taxpayer (ordinary regime at 35% for 2025). Elections available: (1) annual elective entry into the SIMPLE regime (Articles 903-916 ET, Ley 1943/2018 as amended by Ley 2010/2019) for entities with gross ordinary income ≤ 80,000 UVT (approx. COP 3.95 billion for 2025) and ≤ 8 employees; SIMPLE consolidates income tax, a VAT-equivalent component, and industry-and-commerce tax into presumptive tariffs of 1.8%-14.5%, but the taxpayer then charges no VAT and cannot recover input VAT through the ordinary refund mechanics; (2) annual renunciation or withdrawal of SIMPLE with reversion to the ordinary regime; (3) group fiscal consolidation election for qualifying subordinated businesses; (4) CFC rules (Articles 596-600 ET) and hybrid-mismatch rules cannot be neutralised by election.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Financial Superintendence of Colombia, administers the Colombian Foreign Exchange Control Regime under Ley 9 de 1991, Decreto 1735 de 1993, and External Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed floating exchange rate for the Colombian peso (COP). Current-account transactions, including export proceeds, import payments, and cross-border services, are freely convertible but are subject to mandatory channeling through the official exchange market (canalización obligatoria) via authorized foreign exchange intermediaries (intermediarios del mercado cambiario, IMCs). Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment, external credit, and portfolio flows, may be freely made but require registration with Banco de la República and must be settled through an IMC with the corresponding Declaración de Cambio. Profit and dividend remittances to non-residents are unrestricted when paid out of audited post-tax earnings and when the underlying foreign investment registration is current; remittance is executed through an IMC at the prevailing market rate. No mandatory conversion quotas or profit-remittance lockups apply, but unregistered or mis-channeled operations may attract sanctions and loss of exchange-market access for the offending transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters, including a Colombian SAS operating an automated dropshipping model, must collect and channel foreign currency proceeds into Colombia through the official exchange market. The applicable statutory deadlines are 13 months from the date of shipment for exports of goods and 6 months from the date of service provision or billing for exports of services. The full 100% of the export invoice value must be canalized unless the exporter holds a duly authorized compensation account (cuenta de compensación) abroad or relies on an express exemption under Decreto 1735 of 1993. Channeling is perfected by delivering the foreign currency to an IMC and filing the corresponding export declaration and Declaración de Cambio. Late or partial channeling exposes the SAS to monetary fines, possible suspension from the exchange market, and administrative sanction proceedings by Banco de la República; for dropshipping operations, gateway settlement proceeds must be periodically reconciled against underlying customer orders to evidence export provenance and avoid mischaracterization of taxable service income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account - COP Current Account (Cuenta Corriente) with multi-currency and FX sweep capabilities
Operational Account - COP Settlement Account with USD denominated sub-account
Operational Account - COP Transactional Business Account
Operational Account - COP Corporate Account with integrated treasury portal
Operational Account - COP Current Account with trade finance desk
Operational Account - COP Business Account with cross-border wire integration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for principal treasury purposes. Non-resident digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Currencycloud) do not hold Colombian banking licenses and are not authorized to open regulated onshore COP sight accounts or serve as primary treasury vehicles for a Colombian-domiciled SAS. Their use is confined to auxiliary receivable collection or card acquiring support, and any balances must be swept to a local IMC-held account to satisfy the channeling obligation. Colombian-licensed electronic payment institutions (SEDPEs under Ley 1735 of 2014) are legally limited to prepaid, low-value, non-credit instruments and are therefore operationally unsuitable as the treasury backbone. The practical blueprint uses an IMC commercial bank account as the sole FX and liquidity hub.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or video-authenticated interview of the appointed legal representative is mandatory for a corporate account at all tier-1 Colombian banks. If the SAS is managed by a non-resident legal representative, the bank will require either (i) personal appearance at a branch with original identity document, or (ii) a notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of a local attorney or resident representative, plus apostilled corporate documents (articles of incorporation, board resolution appointing officers, good-standing certificate from the Cámara de Comercio) and the valid NIT/RUT tax registration. Fully remote account opening is not available for non-resident-managed SAS entities; the Financial Superintendence's risk-management circulars (Sarlaft) require at least one in-person or digitally-notarized identification event for accounts with wire transfer and FX capability. Appointing a local fiscal representative and a compliance officer materially shortens onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity with micro-ticket values and elevated chargeback ratios typical of automated dropshipping models, flagged by the gateway or bank as potential money-laundering indicators (payment laundering).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier of (1) executed dropshipping supplier agreements with live order-API integration; (2) shipping and logistics proof (carrier tracking records and customs receipts) matching each order; (3) Stripe Radar and PayPal Seller Protection settlement and chargeback reports; (4) audited reconciliation between the order ledger, gateway payout statements, and bank statements; (5) documented refund and return policy with dispute-resolution register; and (6) board minutes approving the dropshipping model as the sole revenue source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) creating discrepancies between the corporate registry, the RUT, and the bank's UBO declaration, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier of (1) a consolidated UBO declaration on the bank's prescribed form identifying all natural persons with more than 5% economic interest; (2) notarized and apostilled identification and proof of residence for each UBO; (3) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence (asset statements, foreign tax returns, capital formation records); (4) the SAS share register (libro de accionistas) with complete transfer history; and (5) audited financial statements of any parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inflows originating from non-bank payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) and foreign card networks being characterized as third-party collections rather than direct customer receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier of (1) gateway merchant agreements and gateway-side KYC records; (2) gateway payout schedules and settlement statements reconciled to the SAS bank account; (3) consolidated gateway invoices and account statements; (4) contractual evidence that the gateway acts solely as settlement agent for the SAS and not as a trading counterparty; (5) a written payment-flow narrative approved by the bank's compliance officer; and (6) periodic board-approved assertion on payment chain integrity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supply-chain exposure to high-risk manufacturing jurisdictions (e.g., suppliers domiciled in China) without demonstrable import documentation for goods ultimately delivered to Colombian or regional consumers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier of (1) pro-forma and final commercial invoices from suppliers; (2) international purchase agreements with Incoterms clauses; (3) bill of lading or airway bills and, where applicable, Colombian customs import declarations; (4) product catalog and barcode mapping between supplier SKUs and the online storefront; (5) bank payment records to suppliers executed via IMCs; and (6) periodic supplier confirmation audits or third-party factory inspection certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions or shareholder loans must be wired by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own foreign bank account to the SAS's IMC-held account. For equity injections, the remittance must be tagged with the proper exchange-market concept code for foreign direct investment and the IMC must receive a Declaración de Cambio identifying the transaction as a capital contribution; the investment must be registered with Banco de la República through the appropriate investment registration form within 12 months of disbursement. For shareholder loans, the external credit must be registered in the external indebtedness regime (régimen de endeudamiento externo) within the legally applicable term, and the funds must be kept segregated from customer operating collections. The compliant path includes: (i) advance verification of the SWIFT beneficiary bank and MT103 field 70 purpose description with the IMC; (ii) use of the direct-investment concept code in the Declaración de Cambio; (iii) certification by the IMC of the FX conversion and issuance of the exchange certificate for DIAN and corporate records; and (iv) refusal of commingled third-party funds to avoid misclassification under Colombian foreign-exchange and tax rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade disbursements use two authorized clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for recurring low-to-mid-value supplier payments, executed by the IMC after verification against matching commercial invoices, purchase orders, and, where required, import declarations; and (ii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit opened by the IMC under UCP 600 for high-value or first-time suppliers, typically confirmed by the supplier's bank. For service imports, including dropship platform commissions and software subscriptions, payments must be supported by a signed service agreement, an electronic invoice, and any applicable withholding tax certificate. Each outbound remittance is accompanied by a Declaración de Cambio; merchandise-related payments must be reconciled with the corresponding Customs import declaration. Where foreign gateways hold settlement currency, the SAS should repatriate balances via the IMC at the prevailing market rate and maintain a distinct reconciliation ledger for each rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore COP/USD forwards (including non-deliverable-style cash-settled forwards referencing the TRM) executed with an authorized IMC.
Exchange-traded USD/COP futures contracts and options on futures on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC) with central counterparty clearing.
Over-the-counter USD/COP call and put options purchased from an authorized IMC, including zero-premium collar structures, for cash-flow hedging of gateway settlements and supplier obligations.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) with an authorized IMC for matched currency and interest-rate risk management on commercial financing.

Regulatory restriction: offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the COP may only be used through an authorized IMC; direct settlement of COP-denominated derivatives with non-resident financial institutions is prohibited absent prior authorization from Banco de la República.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual commercial registration renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 for the current fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal increases the due renewal tariff; two consecutive non-renewals cause suspension and eventual cancellation of the mercantile registration (administrative strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Estados Financieros Certificados (certified annual financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year end (December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit financial statements prevents legal effectiveness against third parties and may block future registration filings; monetary penalties under Chamber of Commerce regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return, Form 110)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between August 9 and August 23 of the following fiscal year, based on the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of 5% of the tax payable per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the tax; default interest of 1.5% per month; administrative strike-off does not apply to tax filings, but collection enforcement and intervention powers of DIAN apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Informe Anual de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO annual reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 1 of each fiscal year, reporting beneficial owners as of the previous December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to 2,000 UVT (approximately USD 34,000) for non-submission or inaccuracies under the Colombian Tax Code; repeated failures may trigger enforced regulation and legal impediments for future corporate acts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal (independent statutory auditor) if: (a) total gross assets at prior year-end exceed 5,000 SMMLV; (b) gross annual revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV; (c) more than 200 employees; or (d) the company is listed on a public securities exchange. For SAS below these thresholds, audit is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Colombia under Decree 2420 of 2015 and subsequent amendments; Group 2 (NIIF para PYMES) for small and medium-sized SAS entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual UBO submission must reflect the full chain of ownership and control as of December 31. Any share transfer must be first recorded in the company's share transfer book and then filed with the Cámara de Comercio to gain enforceability. The annual UBO report serves as the statutory confirmation of the ultimate beneficial ownership and automatically supersedes prior-year data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150 – 400 USD per year (virtual registered office or registered agent service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 800 – 2,500 USD per year for a typical small dropshipping SAS (if mandatory due to thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general territorial tax holidays or legal deductions are available for a standard dropshipping retailer. The only relevant reductions are: (i) 100% deduction of VAT paid on qualifying capital goods destined for infrastructure, and (ii) an incremental 25% income tax deduction for investments in science, technology, and innovation certified by the Ministry of Science. Such incentives do not lower the headline 35% rate for routine e-commerce intermediary income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas), filed electronically through the DIAN MUISCA Portal (panorama fiscal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due annually within the DIAN chronological filing calendar for the relevant tax year. For calendar-year companies, filing opens in the second or third month after the fiscal year-end and closes no later than mid-April of the following year, depending on the last two digits of the NIT (taxpayer identification number).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year (YYYY) and taxpayer abbreviated name and NIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign shareholder never appears on the headline of the form; the Colombian S.A.S. files under its own NIT, with the non-resident beneficial owner disclosed in the annex on shareholders or in Form 220 transfer pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary statutory economic activity code according to DIAN's codebook.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the ISIC 4791 code corresponding to 'Retail sale via mail order houses, internet, or automated dropshipping.' The company must have the correct CIIU registered in the RUT before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross ordinary income from all commercial operations, including dropshipping sales net of discounts and sales returns, converted to COP at the official exchange rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income sourced in Colombia is included. A non-resident facilitated dropship network does not exclude income; attribution of revenue to the Colombian entity follows the substance over form analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: directly allocated costs of goods sold, platform commissions (e.g., Stripe/PayPal fees), logistics costs, and other arms-length operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are only allowed when expenses are proper and were subject to the required withholding tax for cross-border payments. Non-resident suppliers' invoices must prove beneficial ownership and be included in the transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after subtracting deductions, exempt income, and allowable thin-cap limitations from total taxable revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The figure must match the adjusted net profit of the S.A.S. after eliminating artificial mark-ups to related foreign suppliers. A non-resident parent cannot claim fixed deemed deductions on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 47 – Impuesto neto de renta a cargo (35%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The final corporate income tax before prepayments and withholdings. Calculated as 35% of the tax base in Box 46.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian company must apply the 35% rate. No discount is allowed for taxes paid abroad by a non-resident shareholder unless a specific treaty credit mechanism exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 51 – Saldo a pagar / saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between tax payable in Box 47 and prepayments (retentions, self-installments, and credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount must be paid on the same deadline as the return. A failure to remit the balance triggers interest and late-payment penalties, regardless of the foreign shareholder's residency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax payable for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of tax due; if no tax is due, penalty is the greater of 5% of the total gross assets or 1,700 Tax Value Units (UVT). Additional formal penalties under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Statute may apply. Interest accrues at the current official lending rate (2.017% monthly in 2025). Failure to file after DIAN's extended request triggers an automatic penalty of 2% to 5% of the revenue omitted plus imprisonment exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% standard withholding on dividends and other profit-sharing distribution made to non-resident beneficiaries. Where the Colombian company has already paid the 35% corporate income tax, the taxpayer is eligible for a deemed 'fully-taxed profits' deduction, resulting in an effective additional withholding of 0% on that portion. Excess untaxed dividends accrue a 35% withholding taxed at the shareholder level. Thus the headline statutory rate remains 35%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide a valid Certificate of Fiscal Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by the tax authority of the residence state, together with an OECD-compliant declaration of beneficial ownership. The Colombian withholding agent must receive these documents prior to or at the moment of payment to apply the preferential treaty rate (commonly 5%–15% for dividends). The documentation must be maintained by the S.A.S. in its transfer pricing file. For jurisdictions with no DTA, the full 35% statutory rate is withheld and remitted via the MUISCA platform.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 35% for non-resident creditors, reduced to 20% when the creditor is a foreign financial institution registered with the National Securities Registry; treaties often reduce to 10%–15%. Royalties: statutory 35% on payments for IP-use or technical services; DTA protocols typically reduce royalty withholding to 10%–15% depending on the instrument and threshold. All payments are treated as Colombian-source income regardless of the location of intellectual property registration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Copied: mandatory Local File and Master File arise when the Colombian S.A.S. obtains gross income greater than 215,000 UVT (approximately COP 10,500,000,000 for fiscal year 2024). For taxpayers between 125,000 and 215,000 UVT, a simplified TP Informative Return (Form 220) is required. The threshold is inflationary-adjusted annually and must be verified against the applicable fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulation, but the tax administration applies Articles 657 and 658-3 of the Tax Statute and the general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) to disregard transactions lacking business purpose. A pure-channel dropshipping S.A.S. with no employees, no office, no board meeting minutes, and no physical reception of inventory in Colombia may be recharacterized as a transparent intermediary, causing: (i) inclusion of sales revenue at the full gross level; (ii) denial of inter-company commission deductions; and (iii) classification as a 'shell entity' for anti-money laundering and tax evasion purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting dropshipping revenues from Box 35 or recording fake deductions (supplier invoices, warehouse expenses, marketing costs) in Form 210 so as to reduce the 35% income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine under Article 317 of the Colombian Tax Statute equal to 200% of the evaded tax; criminal prosecution under Law 1943 of 2018 carries a prison sentence of 48 to 108 months and a fine from four to twenty-four times the amount evaded, payable in monthly minimum wages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. with no physical presence, no Colombian employees, no real bank account, and no decision-making substance, while converting the legal entity into a mere pass-through for automated dropshipping funds belonging to a foreign principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Courts and DIAN may pray the lifting of the corporate veil under Article 111 of the Commercial Code. The legal entity is disregarded; the shareholder is directly liable for unpaid taxes and liabilities; the foreign principal may be deemed to have a permanent establishment in Colombia with its own income tax assessment at 35% plus additional penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Transfer Pricing Form 220, failing to maintain the Local/Master File, or using a cost-plus mark-up unrelated to the functional and risk profile of an automated e-commerce intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may impose a sanction of 4% of the value of controlled cross-border transactions for each month or fraction of non-submission, with a ceiling of 20,260 UVT (around COP 1,000 million in 2024). If documents are furnished only after a formal evidential notice, an additional fixed penalty of 2,600 UVT (about COP 126 million) applies. The transactions are re-priced to market, increasing the tax debt and liquidity fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payments through Stripe, PayPal or similar rails from undisclosed foreign beneficiaries, using the S.A.S. identity to invoice while concealing the actual beneficial owner, or moving proceeds through multiple low-tax jurisdictions without registering the beneficial ownership report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Law 1843 of 2018 (UIAF anti-money laundering statute) can result in fines up to 1,200,000 tax value units (approx. COP 60,000 million in 2024). Criminal money laundering offences are sanctioned by imprisonment between 10 and 20 years and fines equivalent to up to 2,000,000 minimum statutory monthly wages. Assets traceable to the scheme are subject to civil forfeiture.
